threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop—only to watch it sail by because you weren't waving your arm like it's a flag. Welcome to London!
Caught a night bus to Bermondsey, driver made an impromptu detour to avoid a stag do causing chaos at the stop. Missed my stop but got some free entertainment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: That moment when the kebab shop owner remembers your order and starts making it before you even step in—now that's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a bar with a swing set in the back, where locals sip cocktails and kids play side by side. Pure Berlin charm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their eye roll when the bus gets stuck behind a dog on the tracks. Tourists just look confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Only in SF would a dog on the tracks pause your commute while folks casually debate whose turn it is to scoop. Classic city moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just about the plaça and the squares, but it’s the hidden side streets that tell the real stories of local life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they struggle to pronounce 'Raval'—they say it like 'Ravel.' It’s a small slip, but oh so telling.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for a bus stop sign instead of checking the app. Everyone else knows 'the 30' rolls by every 10 minutes, no need to wait.
Saw a guy on the 35 who’d bought half a dozen pastries from the bakery—said he was 'the king of midnight snacks'. A true Brixton spirit.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a cat lounging on a stack of vinyl in a Kreuzberg record shop; that’s when I knew I’d made it here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous street art festivals springing up overnight, turning blank walls into vibrant galleries before breakfast.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they yearn for the days when taco trucks didn’t have lines stretching to Valencia. Now, it’s a waiting game just for a burrito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop crowd with a ukulele while waiting for the 19. The bus never showed, but his smile made it worth the wait.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think 'El Bosc de les Fades' is authentic. It's a tourist trap; real magic is in the quiet corners of Parc Güell at sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their unshakeable belief that a table in the sun is a guaranteed spot for a good café con leche at any hour.
